scenarios.name: open-input-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the MQOPEN of the request queue answers 2009 (MQOPEN call 2): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: open-output-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the MQOPEN of the reply queue answers 2035 (MQOPEN call 3): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: get-request-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the first MQGET of the request queue answers 2016 (MQGET call 1): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: put-reply-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the MQPUT of the account reply answers 2051 (MQPUT call 1): its non-OK arm

scenarios.name: close-input-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): the input queue's MQCLOSE in 5000-CLOSE-INPUT-QUEUE answers 2009 (MQCLOSE call 1): its non-OK arm; the nested 8000-TERMINATION it PERFORMs closes the three queues and ends the task

scenarios.name: error-put-fails

faults.why: WHEN OTHER: 'ERROR WHILE READING ACCTFILE' to the error queue, then 8000-TERMINATION

scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6072): read-io-error's MQPUT of the error message in 9000-ERROR answers 2051 (MQPUT call 1): its non-OK arm; the nested 8000-TERMINATION it PERFORMs closes the three queues and ends the task

scenarios.name: close-reply-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6967): the reply queue's MQCLOSE in 8000-TERMINATION answers 2009 (MQCLOSE call 2): the WHEN OTHER PERFORMs 8000-TERMINATION again while it is active, which re-closes the input queue (its open flag is never reset) and recurses without end; both sides stop at the PERFORM stack check (register C20), judged up to it

scenarios.name: close-error-fails
scenarios.why: MQ fault (#6967): the error queue's MQCLOSE in 8000-TERMINATION answers 2009 (MQCLOSE call 3): the WHEN OTHER PERFORMs 8000-TERMINATION again while it is active, which re-closes the input queue (its open flag is never reset) and recurses without end; both sides stop at the PERFORM stack check (register C20), judged up to it

notes: CardDemo's MQ account inquiry (transaction CDRA, program COACCT01, app-vsam-mq): each INQA request names an account id; READ ACCTDAT answers it on CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT (NOTFND and another function are replied to as invalid), a SYNCPOINT after each; an I/O error goes to CARD.DEMO.ERROR. acctdata.txt is CardDemo's own data. The queue manager is a stated fact ("mq": its name CSQ1 and CCSID 37 are illustrative, CardDemo fixes neither; the request, reply and error queues the program names), given alike to both sides (register W3). The task is started by the CKTI trigger monitor in production; here its START data is stated: an MQTM ("start_data", CMQTML layout) naming the request queue (W8). The MQ copybooks are GitGalaxy-written stand-ins (W1); every MQI call is an event compared on both sides with its completion and reason code, and the queues the task leaves (its normal end commits it, W5) are compared. A wait on the empty request queue ends at once with MQRC_NO_MSG_AVAILABLE (W2). A failed MQCLOSE's WHEN OTHER PERFORMs 8000-TERMINATION while it is active (a recursive PERFORM, which IBM leaves unpredictable: register C20); the oracle is GnuCOBOL's, whose nested 8000 closes the queues still marked open and ends the task (close-input-fails). A failed close of the reply or error queue re-closes the input queue (its open flag is never reset after its close; 2019), takes WHEN OTHER again and recurses without end: the case runs the oracle with -fstack-check ("perform_stack_check"), and both sides stop at libcob's 255 nested PERFORMs, judged up to that stop (close-reply-fails, close-error-fails; register C20).
